bank_title: SCROTAL TRAUMA ULTRASOUND / DOPPLER — PHRASES BANK

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Blunt blunt trauma to the groin during sports; rule out testicular rupture.

subs.title: Findings
items: Both testes are normal in size, symmetric in appearance, and demonstrate homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity with smooth, intact echogenic contours of the tunica albuginea.
No intratesticular hematoma or parenchymal fracture line is identified.
Both epididymides are unremarkable.
No hematocele or abnormal extra-testicular fluid collection is present.
Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate symmetric, normal low-resistance intratesticular arterial flow bilaterally.
Mild diffuse scrotal wall thickening (6 mm) is noted without discrete mural hematoma.

subs.title: Impression
items: Intact bilateral testes and tunica albuginea with preserved symmetric testicular perfusion; no sonographic evidence of testicular rupture, hematocele, or torsion.
Mild post-traumatic scrotal wall edema.

bank.title: 2. Testicular Rupture (Tunica Albuginea Disruption with Parenchymal Extrusion)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: High-velocity blunt trauma to the right hemiscrotum with severe swelling and ecchymosis.

subs.title: Findings
items: Right Testis: The right testis demonstrates an irregular, deformed contour with a discrete 1.4 cm focal disruption of the anterior tunica albuginea. Heterogeneous testicular parenchyma is seen extruding through the tunical defect into the scrotal sac. Within the right testicular parenchyma, there is a poorly defined heterogeneous avascular zone measuring 2.2 x 1.5 cm representing intratesticular hemorrhage/infarction, with markedly reduced color Doppler flow in the lower pole.
Right Scrotal Sac: Large, complex, multiseptated echogenic hematocele surrounding the right testis.
Left Hemiscrotum: Normal left testis, epididymis, and intact tunica albuginea with normal perfusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Right testicular rupture, evidenced by focal discontinuity of the tunica albuginea, extrusion of testicular parenchyma, focal parenchymal devascularization, and a large complex right hematocele.
Urgent urological surgical exploration is recommended.

bank.title: 3. Testicular Fracture (Linear Parenchymal Tear with Intact Tunica Albuginea)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Blunt scrotal trauma with persistent localized pain.

subs.title: Findings
items: Traversing the mid-pole of the left testis is a well-defined, linear, hypoechoic, avascular band measuring 1.8 cm in length consistent with a parenchymal fracture line.
Color Doppler demonstrates preserved normal vascularity within both the upper and lower poles of the left testis on either side of the fracture cleft.
Careful multiplanar scanning confirms that the overlying echogenic tunica albuginea remains completely intact and smooth without parenchymal extrusion.
A small simple reactive hydrocele is noted.

subs.title: Impression
items: Left testicular parenchymal fracture with preserved bipolar testicular perfusion and an intact tunica albuginea (no testicular rupture).
Small reactive left hydrocele. Urological consultation recommended for close conservative vs. surgical management.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Direct blunt impact to the left testis 24 hours ago.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the upper pole of the left testis, there is a well-circumscribed, round, heterogeneous predominantly hypoechoic lesion measuring 1.6 x 1.4 cm with no internal color Doppler vascularity, consistent with an acute intratesticular hematoma.
The surrounding testicular parenchyma demonstrates normal echogenicity and preserved color Doppler perfusion.
The tunica albuginea is completely intact with a normal smooth testicular contour.
No significant hematocele is present.

subs.title: Impression
items: Isolated left intratesticular hematoma with an intact tunica albuginea and preserved surrounding testicular perfusion.
Serial follow-up ultrasound recommended until complete resolution to exclude an underlying occult neoplasm.

bank.title: 5. Large Complex Hematocele with Intact Testes

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Massive tense scrotal swelling following bicycle handlebar injury.

subs.title: Findings
items: Distending the right hemiscrotum is a large, extra-testicular complex fluid collection containing diffuse low-level internal echoes, thick fibrinous septations, and dependent echogenic clot, consistent with a large acute hematocele.

The right testis is displaced posteriorly and mildly compressed by the hematocele, but maintains a smooth, continuous tunica albuginea, homogeneous internal echogenicity, and symmetric normal intratesticular arterial Doppler flow.

subs.title: Impression
items: Large right complex hematocele exerting mild extrinsic mass effect on the right testis.
Intact right tunica albuginea and preserved testicular vascularity without sonographic evidence of testicular rupture.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Severe acute onset left scrotal pain immediately following a fall.

subs.title: Findings
items: The left testis is enlarged, globally heterogeneous/hypoechoic, and transversely oriented in a high-riding position.
Just superior to the left testis, the spermatic cord demonstrates an abrupt spiral twist ("whirlpool sign") accompanied by an enlarged, congested left epididymal head.
Color and spectral Doppler interrogation reveals complete absence of intratesticular arterial and venous blood flow within the left testis, whereas the right testis demonstrates normal perfusion.
The tunica albuginea is intact.

subs.title: Impression
items: Left testicular torsion (trauma-induced), evidenced by absent left intratesticular Doppler perfusion and a spermatic cord whirlpool sign.
Surgical emergency; immediate urological consultation for emergent detorsion/orchiopexy.

bank.title: 7. Traumatic Epididymal Hematoma / Laceration & Scrotal Wall Hematoma

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Localized left groin pain and palpable lump after blunt trauma.

subs.title: Findings
items: Epididymis: The left epididymal tail is markedly enlarged (measuring 1.8 cm) and heterogeneous with a focal 1.3 x 0.9 cm hypoechoic avascular collection consistent with a traumatic epididymal hematoma, surrounded by mild reactive hyperemia of the adjacent epididymal body.
Scrotal Wall: Focal thickening of the left anterolateral scrotal wall (measuring 14 mm) containing a localized 2.1 x 0.8 cm heterogeneous mural hematoma.
Testes: Both testes and tunica albuginea are completely normal with symmetric Doppler perfusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Traumatic left epididymal tail hematoma and focal left scrotal wall hematoma.
Intact bilateral testes with normal perfusion; no testicular rupture or torsion.
